Title: Collin County teen named Time magazine's 2025 Kid of the Year for bridging digital divides

Summary: 
Tejasvi Manoj, a 17‑year‑old from Collin County, Texas, was named Time magazine’s 2025 Kid of the Year for creating Shield Seniors, an AI‑powered prototype that helps adults 60+ spot and report online scams. The app, inspired by a 2023 incident in which her grandfather almost fell for a scam, uses artificial intelligence to assess whether a message is fraudulent and offers educational content on cybersecurity. According to the article, the Federal Bureau of Investigation reported that losses to internet crime exceeded $16 billion last year, a rise of one‑third since 2023, and the Federal Trade Commission noted that older adults lose far more money in scams than any other age group. Tejasvi says, 'I want to educate these older adults so that they will be able to be more independent online, more confident online,' and that she wants to make them as comfortable as possible. Her mentor, Aarathi Rajamanickam, praised her work, saying, 'It's amazing to see how this young mind was able to take inspiration from that situation and build something.' Her father, Manoj Ganapathy, added, 'It was not easy,' and noted that Tejasvi taught herself the technology. The Time cover shows Tejasvi looking inquisitively ahead with her fist propped beneath her chin. She has received congratulations from Mark Cuban, Gov. Greg Abbott, and actress Priyanka Chopra Jonas. Tejasvi plans to expand Shield Seniors to reach every older adult and is eyeing universities such as MIT, Stanford, and UC Berkeley.

Published date: September 19 2025, 12:06

Title: How AI Can Transform Your Time Management in 2025

Summary: 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is positioned as a transformative tool for time management in 2025, helping individuals optimize their 24-hour days despite competing demands from work, family, and personal goals. AI-powered tools act as smart personal assistants (e.g., Motion, Reclaim.ai, Clockwise) that automate meeting scheduling and task organization by analyzing workloads and identifying optimal times for focus, rest, and collaboration. AI enhances task prioritization through platforms like Notion AI, Todoist AI, and Trello with AI plugins, which assess urgency and importance, reducing decision fatigue. Focus apps such as RescueTime, Focus@Will, and Serene monitor digital habits and provide real-time nudges to maintain concentration, adjusting break suggestions based on attention patterns. Routine planning is streamlined by ClickUp AI and Monday.com AI, which automate reminders, progress tracking, and update summaries, minimizing manual effort. Wellness tools like Calm AI, Headspace AI, and Welltory integrate biometric data (e.g., heart rate, sleep) with calendar insights to recommend personalized breaks, meditation, or walks, supporting mental recovery. The article concludes that AI’s role is not to replace human effort but to reclaim time by enabling smarter work, ultimately allowing individuals to focus on meaningful relationships and goals. The central claim is that 'the best productivity hack isn't working harder — it's working smarter with AI.'
